mainTopic: Defending רבה's five lashes, the ״הואיל״ link to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and how much dough may be kneaded at once on פסח.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא that reads a verse in יחזקאל to learn what may be offered on the מזבח. Two rules come from it: ערלה is nullified in two hundred, and נסכים may not come from טבל, while a מוקצה animal may still be offered. אביי uses the ברייתא to argue that מוקצה is only rabbinic. He also reminds רבה of his own rule that there is no חילוק מלאכות on יום טוב. The גמרא defends רבה's count of five lashes by replacing הבערה, first with עצי אשירה and then, after a challenge from רב אחא בריה דרבא, with עצי הקדש. רמי בר חמא then ties the ״הואיל״ dispute between רב חסדא and רבה to the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about חלה. רב פפא and רב שישא each push back on that link. רבי ירמיה and רבי זירא then argue over whether רבי אליעזר's silence in a ברייתא disproves it. The amud ends with rulings and measures for kneading dough on פסח, and רב's 'Melogna קב', which a ברייתא on the next amud will challenge.

steps.title: ערלה is nullified in two hundred
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads ״מן המאתים״ to teach that wine from a mixture with two hundred permitted parts may be offered, which shows that ערלה is nullified in two hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From the two hundred" means from what is left over of two hundred parts that remained in the vat. From here we learn that ערלה is nullified in two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that אביי is quoting, and it explains the verse one phrase at a time. This phrase teaches the rule that ערלה becomes nullified in a mixture of two hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of offerings coming "from the two hundred." The ברייתא pictures a vat where forbidden ערלה wine got mixed with permitted wine. If there are two hundred permitted parts, the mixture is fine even for the מזבח, so ערלה is בטל in two hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit (or wine) from a tree or vine in its first three years, which is forbidden
Is nullified, meaning it loses its forbidden status in a large mixture
A pit or vat where wine collects

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic invented here. אביי began quoting this ברייתא on the previous amud, and this amud starts in the middle of it.

phrases.english: "From the two hundred" —
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the פסוק in יחזקאל מה:טו.

phrases.english: from the leftover of two hundred parts
that remained in the vat.
From here we learn that ערלה is nullified in two hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that אביי began quoting on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערלה is nullified in a mixture of two hundred.

steps.title: Only what is permitted to a Jew may be offered
steps.stepSummary: From ״ממשקה ישראל״ the ברייתא learns that offerings must come from what is permitted to a Jew, so נסכים cannot come from טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From the drink of Israel" means from what is permitted to Israel. From here they said: we do not bring wine-libations from untithed produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next phrase of the verse. It learns that anything offered must be something a Jew is allowed to eat or drink, so טבל is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״ישראל״ ties the offering to what is permitted for a Jew. טבל is forbidden for a Jew to eat, so wine that is טבל cannot be used for נסכים. This rule becomes the base for the next step about מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The drink of Israel, read as what is permitted to a Jew
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken, so it is forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that אביי will build on. The question that follows is which kinds of forbidden things fall under it.

phrases.english: "From the drink of Israel" —
from what is permitted to Israel.
From here they said:
We do not bring libations from untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next phrase of the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings must come from what is permitted to a Jew, so libations may not come from טבל.

steps.title: מוקצה is still allowed, unlike טבל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a מוקצה animal may still be offered. טבל is forbidden in itself (איסור גופו), while מוקצה is forbidden only because of an outside reason (איסור דבר אחר).
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think one may not bring from מוקצה. You say: just as טבל is special in that its own prohibition caused it, so too anything whose own prohibition caused it is excluded. This leaves out מוקצה, whose own prohibition did not cause it; rather, a prohibition of something else caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the rule of step 2 also blocks a מוקצה animal. It answers no, and draws a line between being forbidden in itself and being forbidden because of something outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is forbidden because of what the food itself is: it has not been tithed. מוקצה is not forbidden because of anything about the animal. It is forbidden only because of an outside rule connected to שבת or יום טוב. So the rule of ״ממשקה ישראל״ excludes only things like טבל, and a מוקצה animal may be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought, which opens a possibility that will be rejected
Something set aside and not prepared for use on שבת or יום טוב
A prohibition built into the item itself
A prohibition that comes from an outside factor

steps.whatToRemember: טבל is excluded because it is forbidden in itself. מוקצה is not excluded because it is forbidden only for an outside reason.

phrases.english: I might think one may not bring from מוקצה.
You say: just as טבל is special
in that its own prohibition caused it —

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר גּוּפוֹ גָּרַם לוֹ.
phrases.english: so too anything whose own prohibition caused it.
This excludes מוקצה,
whose own prohibition did not cause it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לוֹ.
phrases.english: rather, a prohibition of something else caused it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of the rule from step 2 by excluding מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה animal may be offered, because its prohibition comes from an outside factor and not from the item itself.

steps.title: If מוקצה were Torah law, the distinction would mean nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues from the ברייתא that מוקצה must be rabbinic. If it were דאורייתא, the difference between איסור גופו and איסור דבר אחר would make no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that the prohibition of מוקצה is from the Torah, what difference does it make to me whether it is forbidden in itself or forbidden because of something else?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now turns the ברייתא against רבה, who holds that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition. He argues that the ברייתא only makes sense if מוקצה is rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מוקצה were forbidden by the Torah, a מוקצה animal would be forbidden to a Jew just like טבל. Then ״ממשקה ישראל״ should exclude it, no matter why it is forbidden. Since the ברייתא allows it, the real reason must be that מוקצה is only מדרבנן, and the verse only excludes Torah prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, a Torah-level law
What difference is it to me, meaning there should be no difference

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says out loud that מוקצה is rabbinic. אביי is drawing that conclusion from its reasoning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenges רבה's position that one can receive lashes for מוקצה.

phrases.english: And if you say
that the prohibition of מוקצה is from the Torah,
what difference is it to me whether it is forbidden in itself
or forbidden because of something else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's distinction from step 3 as a challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition, so that lashes can be given for it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under a Torah-level מוקצה, both kinds of prohibition would make the animal forbidden to a Jew. The ברייתא's distinction would then be pointless, so מוקצה must be rabbinic.

steps.title: Your own rule: no division of labors on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second challenge. רבה himself said there is חילוק מלאכות for שבת but not for יום טוב, so he cannot count separate lashes for separate acts on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, aren't you the one who said: there is division of labors for שבת, but there is no division of labors for יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, separate objection, this time from רבה's own earlier statement. Since there is no חילוק מלאכות on יום טוב, adding an extra set of lashes for מוקצה alongside cooking on יום טוב does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, each different kind of מלאכה counts on its own for punishment. On יום טוב, רבה said that is not so. So even if מוקצה were a Torah prohibition, the separate יום טוב acts in this case could not each bring their own lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which introduces an additional challenge
Aren't you the one who said, a challenge from the person's own words
Division of labors: each separate kind of מלאכה counts separately for punishment

steps.whatToRemember: אביי attacks רבה twice. First, the ברייתא shows that מוקצה is only rabbinic. Second, רבה's own rule says there is no חילוק מלאכות on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And furthermore, aren't you the one who said:
there is division of labors for Shabbat,
but there is no division of labors for a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an independent second objection against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's counting of a separate set of lashes for מוקצה on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's own principle is that there is no חילוק מלאכות on יום טוב. So separate יום טוב acts cannot each bring their own lashes.

steps.title: Swap kindling for using wood of an idolatrous tree
steps.stepSummary: To keep the ברייתא in line with רבה, the גמרא removes הבערה from the list of five. In its place it puts burning wood of an אשירה, which is forbidden by ״ולא ידבק בידך מאומה מן החרם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, take 'kindling' out of the ברייתא and put in 'wood of an אשירה.' The warning (the לאו) for that comes from the verse 'Nothing from the banned property shall cling to your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by changing one item in the ברייתא's list. The fire was not punished as a separate act of lighting. It was punished because the cook used forbidden idol wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה cannot count separate lashes for lighting on יום טוב. The ברייתא still says 'five,' so the fifth lash must come from somewhere else. If the fire was made from עצי אשירה, benefiting from that wood is its own לאו, so the count of five stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire (one of the forbidden מלאכות)
Wood of a tree worshipped as an idol
The warning, meaning the negative commandment needed before lashes can be given

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is changing one item in the ברייתא's list (אפיק ... ועייל, 'take out ... put in') so that it fits רבה's view. The total of five lashes stays the same; only the identity of one לאו changes.

phrases.english: Rather, remove 'kindling,'
and insert 'wood of an asheira.'
phrases.notes: The fire was lit with wood from a tree used for idol worship.

phrases.english: And the warning comes from here:
'And there shall not cling to your hand'
'anything of the banned property.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is דברים 13:18, talking about the spoils of an עיר הנדחת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַפֵּיק הַבְעָרָה, וְעַיֵּיל עֲצֵי אֲשֵׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 5 by re-reading the ברייתא's list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation / re-identification of one item in the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth lash is for הבערה on יום טוב, which would contradict רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth lash is for using עצי אשירה, so it does not depend on separate מלאכות on יום טוב.

steps.title: Idol wood would bring a sixth lash
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא objects that bringing idol wood into one's home also breaks ״ולא תביא תועבה אל ביתך״. That would make six sets of lashes, not five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to אביי: Then he should also get lashes for 'Do not bring an abomination into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised against the answer we just heard. Idol wood carries two לאוין, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cook used עצי אשירה, he also broke the לאו of bringing a תועבה home. That adds another set of lashes. The ברייתא clearly says 'five,' so the idol-wood answer gives the wrong count.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Abaye:
Then let him also be lashed
because of 'You shall not bring an abomination into your house.'
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק in דברים 7:26, so it would be an extra, sixth לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the עצי אשירה answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the fifth lash is for עצי אשירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Idol wood carries an additional לאו (לא תביא תועבה), which would raise the count to six. That contradicts the ברייתא's explicit number of five.

steps.title: Swap kindling for burning sacred wood instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replaces הבערה with burning עצי הקדש. The warning comes from ״לא תעשון כן לה׳ אלהיכם״, which forbids destroying holy things. This adds only one לאו, so the count stays at five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, remove 'kindling' and insert 'wood of הקדש.' The warning comes from here: 'And burn their אשירות in fire... Do not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better replacement for the fifth lash. The fire was made from wood belonging to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning holy wood is destroying a sacred object. That is forbidden by one לאו, learned from 'do not do so to ה׳,' meaning do not destroy His things the way you destroy idols. Since there is only one לאו, the ברייתא keeps exactly five, and רבה is no longer contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood consecrated to the בית המקדש
Do not do so, meaning do not destroy holy things the way you destroy idols

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of five lashes no longer disproves רבה. Its fifth lash is for burning הקדש wood, not for a separate act of lighting on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rather: remove 'kindling,'
and insert 'consecrated wood.'
And the warning comes from here:
'And their asheira trees you shall burn in fire...'
'You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
phrases.notes: This is דברים 12:3-4, which teaches that destroying holy things is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַפֵּיק הַבְעָרָה, וְעַיֵּיל עֲצֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's objection by choosing a replacement that carries only one לאו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Revised emendation of the ברייתא's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth lash is for עצי אשירה, which would actually yield six.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth lash is for burning עצי הקדש, a single לאו, so the count stays at five and רבה stands.

steps.title: The הואיל dispute is an older dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the argument between רב חסדא and רבה is the same as the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אליעזר uses the reasoning of ״הואיל״ and רבי יהושע does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: The dispute of רב חסדא and רבה is really the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אליעזר holds we say 'since' (הואיל), and רבי יהושע holds we do not say 'since.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רמי בר חמא ties the אמוראים' argument to an argument of תנאים in the משנה about separating חלה on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה uses ״הואיל״: since the food could be served to guests, cooking it on יום טוב is not punished. רב חסדא rejects that. רמי בר חמא says רבי אליעזר also relies on ״הואיל״ in the חלה case: since any part of the dough could be freed by separating חלה from another part, one may bake it first. רבי יהושע does not accept that reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since.' Reasoning that something counts as permitted because it could become permitted or useful

steps.confusionAlert: ״הואיל״ is a principle, not a person or a case. It means 'since it could have been permitted, we treat it as permitted.'
steps.whyThisMatters: If the אמוראים are only repeating a dispute of תנאים, then each side has backing from a משנה authority. The גמרא will next check whether this link is really correct.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
This dispute of Rav Chisda and Rabba

phrases.aramaic: מַחֲלוֹקֶת דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא.
phrases.english: is the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.
For Rabbi Eliezer holds:
we say 'since.'
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
we do not say 'since.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה מַחֲלוֹקֶת דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה against the ברייתא, the גמרא opens a new line that roots the whole dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רב חסדא and רבה dispute about ״הואיל״ matches the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע dispute. רבי אליעזר applies ״הואיל״ and רבי יהושע does not.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי אליעזר might not use this reasoning in our case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that רבי אליעזר may use ״הואיל״ only for the חלה case, where every loaf was fit for the baker himself. Bread fit only for guests may be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Maybe רבי אליעזר only uses ״הואיל״ in the חלה case, because when the loaves went into the oven, each one was fit for the baker himself. But here, the bread is fit only for guests, not for him. Maybe even רבי אליעזר would not say ״הואיל״ here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רמי בר חמא. He says רבי אליעזר's case and our case may not be alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חלה case, the baker had not yet chosen which loaf would be חלה, so while baking, every loaf could still be his. In the case of baking on יום טוב for a weekday, the extra bread only helps if guests come; the baker himself does not need it today. So the ״הואיל״ is weaker, and רבי אליעזר may not apply it.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe / perhaps (a word used to push back on a claim)
He only said his rule in that specific case

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Eliezer only said
there that we say "since"
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of separating חלה from impure dough on יום טוב.

phrases.english: because at the time they go into the oven

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא חַזְיָא לֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: each and every one is fit for him himself.
But here, where it is fit for guests
but not fit for him —
say that here too we do not say "since."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְדִילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's claim that רבה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between רבה's view and רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חלה case has a stronger ״הואיל״ (fit for the baker himself) than baking for possible guests, so רבי אליעזר's ruling may not carry over.

steps.title: רב שישא: רבי יהושע might accept this reasoning in our case
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי argues the other side. רבי יהושע may reject ״הואיל״ only because the חלה is fit for no one. Bread fit for guests may be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: Maybe that is not right. רבי יהושע only refuses to use ״הואיל״ in the חלה case, because one piece (the טמא חלה) is fit neither for the baker nor for guests. But here, the bread is at least fit for guests. Maybe even רבי יהושע would say ״הואיל״ here.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא pushes back on רמי בר חמא, this time from רבי יהושע's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טמא חלה cannot be eaten by anyone, so no ״הואיל״ can make baking it count as food preparation. Bread baked on יום טוב for a weekday can at least feed guests who might come. So רבי יהושע may agree to ״הואיל״ here, and the two arguments would not match.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
Perhaps that is not so;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said
there that we do not say "since"
because there is one piece

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא חַזְיָא לָא לְדִידֵיהּ וְלָא לְאוֹרְחִין.
phrases.english: that is fit neither for him nor for guests.
phrases.notes: The impure challah cannot be eaten by anyone.

phrases.english: But here, where it is at least fit for guests —
say that here too we do say "since."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: וְדִילְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel rejection of רמי בר חמא, this time from רבי יהושע's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between רב חסדא's view and רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע's case involves food fit for no one at all, while our case involves food fit at least for guests.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's idea is brought before two sages
steps.stepSummary: The scholars told רמי בר חמא's explanation to רבי ירמיה and רבי זירא. רבי ירמיה accepted it and רבי זירא did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said this (רמי בר חמא's explanation) in front of רבי ירמיה and רבי זירא. רבי ירמיה accepted it. רבי זירא did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up the next move. Two sages react differently to רמי בר חמא's explanation, and we are about to hear why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אמרוה״ ("they said it") refers to רמי בר חמא's claim that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about ״הואיל״. This line only sets the scene; the reasons come in the next two steps.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before
Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Zeira.
Rabbi Yirmeya accepted it;
Rabbi Zeira did not accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רמי בר חמא's explanation (Step 9) and records how later sages reacted to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ירמיה accepts רמי בר חמא's explanation and רבי זירא rejects it.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: Why reject an answer to an old puzzle?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא. For years we did not know what רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about. Now a great man has explained it, so we should accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: For many years we were bothered by the question of what רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about. Now someone has explained it in the name of a great man. Shouldn't we accept it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes רבי זירא to accept רמי בר חמא's explanation. It finally solves a question that bothered them for years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question sounds like it is asking something, but it is really a challenge. רבי ירמיה is saying it is unreasonable to throw away a good explanation from a great scholar when we had no other answer. He puts the burden on רבי זירא to show why it is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that was difficult for us

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
A matter that was difficult for us
and has gone on for several years —

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: about what Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree —
now they have said it in the name of a great man,
and shall we not accept it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: מִילְּתָא דְּקַשְׁיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי ירמיה explains why he accepted the teaching and challenges רבי זירא for rejecting it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's refusal to accept רמי בר חמא's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation solves a long-standing puzzle and comes from a great scholar, so rejecting it needs a strong reason.

steps.title: רבי זירא: רבי אליעזר's silence disproves the explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא cites a ברייתא. רבי יהושע told רבי אליעזר that he violates ״לא תעשה כל מלאכה״, and רבי אליעזר was silent. If ״הואיל״ were his reason, he would have answered with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא answered him: How can I accept it? We learned in a ברייתא: רבי יהושע said to רבי אליעזר, "According to you, this person breaks the rule 'Do not do any work' (on יום טוב)." And רבי אליעזר was silent. If רמי בר חמא were right, רבי אליעזר should have answered: "My reason is ״הואיל״."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה with a ברייתא that he says disproves רמי בר חמא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said that baking טמא חלה, which no one can eat, is forbidden work on יום טוב. With ״הואיל״, רבי אליעזר would have had an easy answer: each loaf could still have been his own food, so the baking counts as permitted food preparation. Since he stayed silent, ״הואיל״ was apparently not his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: And he was silent to him

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר's silence is not just a detail of the story. In the גמרא, when a sage is challenged and stays silent, it usually means he had no answer. That is why רבי זירא uses the silence as evidence against רמי בר חמא.
steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר חמא tied the יום טוב baking argument to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רב פפא and רב שישא each showed the cases may differ. רבי זירא then argued from רבי אליעזר's silence that ״הואיל״ was never his reason.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can I accept it,
for we learned:
Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם ״לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כׇל מְלָאכָה״,
phrases.english: he transgresses "You shall not do any work,"
and he (Rabbi Eliezer) was silent.
But if it were so, let him say to him:
My reason is because of "since."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge by giving a source-based reason to reject רמי בר חמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that רבי אליעזר's view rests on ״הואיל״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״הואיל״ were רבי אליעזר's reason, he could easily have answered רבי יהושע's challenge. His silence shows it was not his reasoning.
steps.whyThisMatters: רמי בר חמא's reading can survive only if רבי אליעזר's silence is explained. Steps 15-16 do this by showing that silence in one source proves nothing.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה turns the silence argument around
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה points to a parallel case. In a ברייתא, רבי יהושע was silent when רבי אליעזר challenged him. But in the משנה, רבי יהושע clearly does answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: By your logic, look at the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר told רבי יהושע, "By your view, he violates בל יראה and בל ימצא," and רבי יהושע was silent. Would you also say רבי יהושע had no answer? But he does answer in the משנה: "This is not the חמץ we are warned about with בל יראה and בל ימצא!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's proof from silence. He shows a case where someone was silent in a ברייתא but clearly had an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said: since רבי אליעזר stayed silent, he must not have had the ״הואיל״ answer. רבי ירמיה replies that silence in a ברייתא cannot mean "no answer." רבי יהושע was also silent in a ברייתא, yet the משנה records his reply.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a formula that turns someone's own logic against them
The prohibitions against having חמץ seen or found in one's possession on פסח
He was silent toward him (gave no recorded reply)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two challenges. In step 14, רבי יהושע challenged רבי אליעזר about baking on יום טוב (״לא תעשה כל מלאכה״). Here it is the reverse: רבי אליעזר challenges רבי יהושע about owning חמץ (בל יראה). Each was silent in one ברייתא.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Yirmeya) said to him: And according to your reasoning,
that which we learned in a baraita,
Rabbi Eliezer said to him: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא״,
phrases.english: he transgresses 'it shall not be seen and it shall not be found,'
phrases.notes: This is if he lets the impure חלה dough become חמץ, as רבי יהושע allows.

phrases.english: and he (Rabbi Yehoshua) was silent.
So too, did he not answer him?
But he does answer him in the Mishnah!
As we learned: This is not the chametz

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא״,
phrases.english: about which we are warned with 'it shall not be seen and it shall not be found.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי זירא's proof from silence in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that רבי אליעזר's silence shows he did not hold ״הואיל״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel case shows silence in a ברייתא even though an answer exists elsewhere, so silence proves nothing.

steps.title: Silence in one place, an answer in another
steps.stepSummary: The principle is that a תנא may be silent in one source and answer in another. So רבי אליעזר may be silent in the משנה and answer in a different tractate. This removes רבי זירא's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say: he was silent in the ברייתא but answered in the משנה. So too here: say רבי אליעזר was silent in the משנה and answered in a different tractate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה draws his conclusion. רבי אליעזר's silence here does not mean he lacked the ״הואיל״ answer, because he may have given it elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבי יהושע's reply appears only in the משנה, רבי אליעזר's reply may appear only in another collection of teachings. The גמרא does not say where that reply is or quote it. Its point is only that silence in one source proves nothing, so רבי זירא's proof against רמי בר חמא's explanation falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A different tractate (a different collection of teachings)

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbi's silence in one source is weak evidence. His answer may be recorded somewhere else. This keeps רמי בר חמא's ״הואיל״ explanation standing.

phrases.english: Rather: he was silent to him in the baraita,
but answered him in the Mishnah.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי, אֵימוֹר שְׁתֵיק לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתִין,
phrases.english: So too, say he was silent to him in the Mishnah,
and answered him in a different tractate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי ירמיה's argument begun in step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זירא's proof from silence entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that silence in one source means there was no answer at all

steps.title: Two rulings on impure חלה on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי rules like רבי אליעזר, while רבי יצחק rules like בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי says the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, and רבי יצחק says the הלכה follows בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opinions on how the הלכה is decided in the משנה's argument about impure חלה on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says to bake everything first and only then separate the חלה. בן בתירא says to put the dough in cold water so it does not become חמץ. רבי and רבי יצחק each rule like a different one of these views.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) says:
The halakha is like Rabbi Eliezer,
and Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The halakha is like ben Beteira.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the theory discussion and gives practical rulings on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי rules like רבי אליעזר (bake, then separate). רבי יצחק rules like בן בתירא (cold water).

steps.title: How much dough may be kneaded at once on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what size of dough is allowed. רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says two קבין of wheat or three of barley. רבי נתן, quoting רבי אליעזר, says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: How large may a dough be? רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: for wheat, two קבין; for barley, three קבין. רבי נתן says in the name of רבי אליעזר: it is the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the largest amount of dough one may knead at once on פסח without worrying it will become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large dough is hard to work quickly, so it risks rising. The two views disagree about which grain allows the larger amount. One says barley allows more (three vs. two). רבי נתן says wheat allows more.

keyTerms.meaning: Kav measures (a unit of volume); here it means two kav

phrases.english: And how much is the measure of a dough?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
With wheat — two kav.
And with barley — three kav.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
The matters are reversed.
phrases.notes: Reversed means: three קבין for wheat and two קבין for barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the size of dough on פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: wheat two קבין, barley three. רבי נתן in the name of רבי אליעזר: the reverse.

steps.title: A conflicting version of רבי ישמעאל's measure
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא quotes the same רבי ישמעאל with larger amounts: three קבין of wheat and four of barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in another ברייתא that רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: for wheat, three קבין; for barley, four קבין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The same rabbi seems to give two different amounts in two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that barley allows one קב more than wheat. But the actual numbers differ (2/3 vs. 3/4). The גמרא needs to explain how one rabbi could say both.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
With wheat — three kav,
and with barley — four kav!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the numbers given in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The 2/3 קבין measure attributed to רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same תנא gives different numbers in two ברייתות.

steps.title: Poor grain versus good grain
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The larger measure (three and four) is for poor-quality grain. The smaller measure (two and three) is for good-quality grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about poor-quality grain, and that one is about good-quality grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two ברייתות speak about different kinds of grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poor grain has more chaff, so it gives less flour per קב. You need more קבין of poor grain to reach the same amount of flour. So both numbers describe the same real amount of dough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (formula for resolving a contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: The real limit is the amount of flour in the dough, not the number of קבין of grain. Poor grain needs more קבין to give that same amount of flour.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one (three/four) refers to poor-quality grain,
that one (two/three) refers to good-quality grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות give conflicting amounts for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא describes a different grain quality, so both give the same amount of flour.

steps.title: Poor wheat is further below good wheat than poor barley is below good barley
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns a side lesson from Step 20. The gap between poor and good wheat (a third) is bigger than the gap between poor and good barley (a quarter).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that poor wheat is worse compared to good wheat than poor barley is compared to good barley. For there (wheat) the difference is one-third, and here (barley) it is only one-quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the answer from Step 20 and draws a new point from the numbers. He compares how big a 'quality gap' wheat has against how big a gap barley has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For wheat, good grain needs 2 קבין and poor grain needs 3. The extra 1 is a third of 3. For barley, good grain needs 3 קבין and poor grain needs 4. The extra 1 is only a quarter of 4. So switching from good to poor quality changes wheat more than it changes barley.
steps.confusionAlert: Both differences are exactly one קב, so it can look as if they are equal. רב פפא is measuring the gap as a fraction of the larger amount: 1 out of 3 for wheat, but only 1 out of 4 for barley.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this
that poor-quality wheat is inferior
to good-quality wheat by more
than poor-quality barley is inferior
to good-quality barley.
For there (with wheat) it is a third,
phrases.notes: Going from 2 to 3: the extra 1 is a third of 3.

phrases.english: and here (with barley) it is a quarter.
phrases.notes: Going from 3 to 4: the extra 1 is a quarter of 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side inference from the numbers used in the answer of Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The quality gap for wheat (one-third) is larger than the quality gap for barley (one-quarter).

steps.title: רב's measure: a Melogna קב for פסח and for חלה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one 'Melogna קב' is the amount of dough to knead at once for פסח. The same amount is the minimum that obligates חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A קב by the measure of Melogna is the amount for פסח dough, and the same amount applies to חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical, single measure for the dough discussion. He also links it to the amount of dough that requires separating חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the separate wheat and barley numbers from the ברייתות, רב names one fixed amount, a קב of Melogna. He says the same amount sets the minimum dough for the חלה obligation. So one measure answers both questions.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a unit of volume for grain or flour
Of Melogna: a place whose קב measure is used here
פסח (here, the matzah dough for פסח)
The portion of dough given to a כהן; also the minimum dough that obligates it

steps.whyThisMatters: Linking the פסח dough size to the חלה minimum ties together two separate halachic measures. The challenge that follows targets exactly this link.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A kav of Melogna is the amount for Passover dough,
and likewise for challah (the minimum that obligates it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא numbers to a new practical ruling by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Melogna קב is the measure for פסח dough and also the minimum for חלה.

steps.title: Opening a challenge to רב from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב with 'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' The ברייתא itself appears on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא...?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to quote a ברייתא that seems to conflict with רב's ruling, and the quote comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase והתניא always signals that a תנאי source is about to contradict what was just said. We will only see what the ברייתא says, and how it conflicts with רב, on the next amud.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: The content of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to challenge רב's ruling from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a Melogna קב is the measure for both פסח and חלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (quoted next) seems to give a different measure, which would contradict רב.
